New Mexico — Cannabis and Hemp Research: Audited and Corrected

Last audited: 31 October 2026 (audit checks 31 October–1 November 2026)  |  Original research date: 31 October 2026  |  This file is the independent audit and the corrected rewrite of the complete Parts 0–12 dossier, in one self-contained document.

Scope. The auditor did not write the original report. Every factual claim in Parts 0–12 was checked against primary sources only: the New Mexico Statutes Annotated (via NMOneSource), bill pages on nmlegis.gov, the New Mexico Administrative Code and New Mexico Register, the RLD Cannabis Control Division (licensee lists, enforcement actions, dashboards), the Department of Health Medical Cannabis Program, the Taxation and Revenue Department, NMED, NMDA, the Office of the State Engineer, Attorney General opinions, New Mexico courts, official tribal and pueblo government sources and intergovernmental-agreement texts, and official county and municipal sites and codes. Nothing was confirmed from news, law-firm blogs, trade press or AI summaries alone; where only a secondary source exists, the claim is marked Unverified.

Federal baseline — given, not re-audited

  • Split scheduling: under a final rule at 91 FR 22714 (effective 28 April 2026), FDA-approved cannabis products and state-licensed medical marijuana are in Schedule III. All other marijuana, including all adult-use, remains Schedule I. The broader 2024 rescheduling proposal is NOT final.
  • IRS §280E: Treasury has said rescheduling generally removes §280E as a bar for businesses no longer dealing in Schedule I/II substances (guidance forthcoming). Adult-use activity remains fully subject to §280E.
  • Hemp: Public Law 119-37 §781 takes legal effect 12 November 2026, but Public Law 119-103 §2019 limits it until 11 December 2026 to only the provisions excluding cannabinoids that are not naturally produced or are synthesized. The full total-THC definition and 0.4 mg per container cap apply after 11 December 2026.
  • USDA has delayed enforcement of the DEA-registered-laboratory hemp testing requirement until 31 December 2026.
  • The federal medical-marijuana appropriations rider is in force through 11 December 2026.
  • No federal cannabis banking law has been enacted.

New Mexico application. Schedule III status and the §280E change apply to medical activity only. Businesses serving both markets must split their activity; all adult-use activity remains Schedule I and fully subject to §280E. Whether any medical activity by a tribal operation under an intergovernmental agreement counts as “state-licensed” under the federal rule is Verify throughout this file — it is not answered by the sources opened, and no tribal operator should be told it has Schedule III/§280E relief on this basis. New Mexico's 20 mg/package hemp cap is 50× the federal 0.4 mg/container cap, so state compliance does not guarantee federal compliance after 11 December 2026. No New Mexico response to the federal 12 November / 11 December 2026 hemp dates was found as of 31 October 2026.

Audit method and limits — read before relying on this file

  • Verdict counts (recounted by the assembler from the audit tables in Part 1): Confirmed 379, Corrected 215, Removed 12, Unverified 401 — total 1007 rows. Segment totals: Parts 0–1: 261 (123/55/1/82); Parts 2–4: 153 (57/17/3/76); Parts 5–7: 117 (49/28/3/37); Parts 8–10: 242 (35/49/1/157); Parts 11–12: 234 (115/66/4/49). The high Unverified share is structural: the original itself ran no assessor/zoning/parcel search for any Part 8 property, opened no IGA text, and many tribal, checkpoint and polling claims rest on secondary sources; most Part 3 jurisdiction rows rest on codes that were not opened in either the original run or this audit.
  • NMOneSource limitation (the single largest residual item): many statute texts were read on Justia/LawServer/Cornell mirrors, not by direct NMOneSource opens. Every mirror-text confirmation therefore carries an NMOneSource re-check in the still-unverified list. No NMOneSource section URL was invented.
  • Live-dashboard limitation: a live fetch of the CCD CROP dashboard during the audit returned only a filtered view ($488,330,327.43), not the headline sales series. Sales, licence-count and city-total figures that rest on press/index reporting of CROP data are therefore labelled secondary, not official, even where their arithmetic reconciles.
  • Cross-segment resolutions applied by the assembler (not counted in the 1,007 audit rows, listed here so they are not silent): (1) front-matter sales figures labelled secondary, not official; (2) latest official patient figure set to August 2026, 60,501, not July 60,400; (3) producer per-plant fees confirmed at 16.8.11.11 NMAC, replacing the front matter's “Part 11 did not re-verify” note; (4) the stray Parts 11–12 bridge heading at the end of the Parts 8–10 fragment removed (full Parts 11–12 follow); (5) “[AUDIT CORRECTION]” markers stripped from the Parts 11–12 text so the rewrite reads as one document (the audit table remains the authoritative record); (6) the original final Research Notes section, which no segment fragment included, is restored at the end of the rewrite with the audit corrections applied in place to its superseded items (HB 346, NMDA fees, NMED fees, GRT-on-excise, producer tiers, reciprocity/consumption citations, buffers, firearms, patient and sales totals, testing-table currency, Bluebonnet hold).
  • Personal contacts: no personal phone number or email of an individual licence holder is reproduced in this file. Agency programme contacts published by the agencies themselves are retained where the original gave them. Same-name places are kept apart throughout (Las Vegas NM vs NV, Santa Fe NM vs TX, Roswell NM vs GA, Clovis NM vs CA, Carlsbad NM vs CA, Socorro NM vs TX, Artesia NM vs CA, Anthony NM vs Anthony TX, Sunland Park NM vs El Paso TX vs Ciudad Juárez).

Headline corrections

  • Sales are no longer presented as official totals. July 2026 ($49,814,500.78) and all-time April 2022–July 2026 ($2,406,115,223.06) could not be verified on the live CROP dashboard and are secondary reporting of CCD data. No official annual sales total is adopted for 2024 ($540m/$580m/$590m, all secondary) or 2025 ($567–568m secondary; $628m rejected as uncorroborated). The all-time transaction split does not sum (54,027,968 stated vs 54,998,714 components) and the June 2026 transaction conflict (842,530 vs 918,523) is unresolved.
  • Patients: latest official DOH figure is August 2026, 60,501 (data as of 2 September 2026), superseding July 2026, 60,400, as “latest.” May 2026, 60,344, is DOH-confirmed. September 2026, 60,720, remains secondary/unverified.
  • Licence counts: 3,071 approvals are a secondary compilation with a date conflict (May/June 2026 vs 4 December 2024 — neither adopted as official), and the June 2025 premises breakdown (303/274/687/317/27/7/0) is likewise secondary reporting of CCD data, not an official CCD figure. No current September/October 2026 active-licence count by type and status is available.
  • Part 8 properties: strict verified count is 0. Every Table A/B “zoning” entry is a listing-agent/broker claim only and is downgraded to CONDITIONAL. Headline total corrected from 39 to 38 marketed presentations (29 address-identified + 9 no-address); B10 (Sandia Botanicals, Las Cruces, $60,000) is removed as a business/asset sale on a leased site. Albuquerque count corrected 13 to 11 of 29.
  • Fictitious hemp ratio removed: there is no 15:1 CBD:Total THC ratio in 20.10.2 NMAC. 20.10.2.12(A) contains paragraphs (1)–(3) only: ≤0.30% total THC, ≤2 mg/serving, ≤20 mg/package (tinctures ≤100 mg/package; broad-spectrum ≤6.0 mg/package; cosmetics/vapes exempt from the mg caps only).
  • NMDA hemp fees resolved: 2026 Annual form $650 + $6.00/acre + $10/variety; Continuous $750 + $0.75/1,000 sq ft + $10/variety — both below the 21.20.2.10 rule ceilings ($800/$900). Only the legal basis of the $10 varietal minimum (vs $25 per variety in excess of one in the rule) remains Verify.
  • NMED hemp permits confirmed and counted: 20.10.2.8 fees/terms/transfer/renewal confirmed from the published final rule ($1,000/$1,000/$1,000/$500, late $200, reinspection $500, variance $300, anniversary-month expiry, non-transferable). Official NM Approved Hemp Facilities list, 26 October 2026: 36 facilities (19 manufacturing-type, 17 warehouse-type, 1 extraction facility, one combined facility counted once) — correcting the June 2026 secondary warehouse count of 10 to 17 and contradicting the original §5.8 claim that no list exists. No entry is labelled “Retail Manufacturer.”
  • Converted-cannabinoid exception completed: the ≥98% purity list in 20.10.2.11(L) is nine items (THCV, CBC, CBT, CBL, CBE, CBG, CBDV, CBD, CBN), not four. The ban binds a “hemp facility” (including one selling imported converted product) but does not on its face bind a pure retailer, which is not a “hemp facility.”
  • HB 346 (2025) is dead, not a proposal and not pocket-vetoed: House 54–7 (13 March 2025), Senate 37–0 as amended (22 March 2025), then Action Postponed Indefinitely, no House concurrence. Its NMED/EIB transfer never took effect.
  • GRT resolved: gross receipts tax excludes cannabis excise tax receipts from 1 July 2023 (TRD FYI-260, Rev. 07/2026, p. 4). FY2027 combined GRT range is 5.25%–9.4375% (replacing the FY2026 maximum of 10.8125% as current). The October 2025 TRD “missing file” gap is deleted (file-naming confusion).
  • Producer tiers resolved: Level 1 is 201–2,000 mature plants, increases in 500-plant increments, on current SRCA 16.8.8.9 text. The 401 lower bound and 1,000-plant increment were 13 January 2022 emergency-amendment figures only. Section 26-2C-40 was NOT repealed on 31 December 2025 — the scheduled repeal was itself repealed by Laws 2024, ch. 38, §19.
  • Testing Table 1 is obsolete: the 31 August 2026 amendment (NM Register Vol. XXXVII, Issue 16) replaces the product categories; the former pesticide exception (E)(1) was deleted. There IS a general recall rule, 16.8.2.11, and 24-hour failed-product notice is in 16.8.7.15(O). There is no pesticide-failure remediation route — pesticide failures go to destruction.
  • Firearms decided: United States v. Hemani, 608 U.S. 772 (18 June 2026), did not strike down 18 U.S.C. §922(g)(3) (as-applied only). Schedule III status alone does not remove the disability. ATF interim final rule, 91 FR 2698 (eff. 22 January 2026), defines “unlawful user” as regular use over an extended period continuing into the present without a lawful prescription.
  • Tribal citation trap corrected: §26-2C-38 is “Imports and exports” (dormant interstate framework); §26-2C-41 is the tribal intergovernmental-agreement section. Only Picuris and Pojoaque IGAs are sourced (announced 25 March 2022); full texts remain unavailable, every IGA term (tax, testing, tracking, trade, regulator, who may buy) remains Verify, and the tribal “state-licensed” Schedule III/§280E question stays Verify — §26-2C-41 does not deem tribal licensees CCD licensees.
  • CRA range corrected: as enacted by HB 2 the Cannabis Regulation Act is §§26-2C-1 to -42, not -43; §26-2C-43 was added later by HB 10 (2025). §26-2C-42 (“Cooperation of agencies”) is resolved. SB 6 (2024) drive-up window ban is NOT law — the prohibition was removed by floor amendment and is not in enacted ch. 38.
  • Recalls corrected: February 2026 was not the only recall. RLD lists four mandatory recalls: 22 March 2024, 6 September 2024 (Maggie's Farm), 27 November 2024 (Stash House), 26 February 2026 (GH Kush Pops). Bluebonnet Labs' hold continued (Bulletin 25-19, 13 November 2025, plus Permanent Restraining Order D-202-CV-2025-00809).
  • Expungement: no official cumulative total exists. ~14,000 (April 2023, AOC via press) and the 151,640/155,000 pool are secondary-only and must never be presented as a 2026 total. Follow-up: direct AOC/DPS request under §29-3A-8.
  • SB 323 (2019) corrected: up to ½ oz is a $50 penalty assessment (payment is not a criminal conviction), not a petty misdemeanor; the $50–$100 petty-misdemeanor range is the next tier (over ½ oz to 1 oz, first offense).
  • U.S. Eagle / Aery no longer available (announced 1 November 2026 shutdown has passed) and must not be listed as a current banking option. Other named banks remain vendor-list/institution-claim only (Unverified onboarding).

PART 1 — AUDIT

One verdict per row: Confirmed (checks out against a primary source actually opened), Corrected (wrong, misleadingly framed or superseded, with the correct version stated), Removed (wrong and no correct version found), Unverified (only a secondary source exists, or no primary source could be opened). Source links are given per row; where the source is a search-index excerpt, a mirror, or a dashboard with no download, the row says so.

§0.1The NMED ban does not by itself ban imported finished products sold at retail; that gap was expressly noted in contemporaneous legal commentary and is Verify against the final rule textCorrected20.10.2.7(X) and (FF) (final-rule PDF, same URL as above)Narrowed: on the rule's face the §8(K) ban binds hemp facilities (extraction, manufacturing, warehouse, retail manufacturer — 20.10.2.7(X)); a mere retailer is not listed as a facility (hemp retailer is defined separately at 20.10.2.7(FF)). Whether mere retail sale of imported converted-cannabinoid products is banned remains Verify against the full rule text and any NMED guidance, and must not be stated either way.

§1.5Statutory hemp definition (§76-24-4): Cannabis sativa L. and any part thereof, including seeds and all derivatives, extracts, cannabinoids, isomers, acids, salts and salts of isomers, whether growing or not, with THC concentration not more than 0.3% (on a dry-weight basis; the bracket in the HB 346 bill text shows the dry-weight phrase as existing law)ConfirmedHB 346 bill text showing the existing definition (https://www.nmlegis.gov/sessions/25%20Regular/bills/house/HB0346.PDF); NMOneSource re-check of the unamended §76-24-4 text still requiredAs stated. Re-check the unamended §76-24-4 text on NMOneSource before quoting it verbatim.
§1.5Cannabis vs hemp threshold (§26-2C-2): cannabis means genus Cannabis containing more than 0.3% delta-9 THC on a dry-weight basis; at or below 0.3% delta-9, the plant / material is hemp, not cannabis, for CRA purposesConfirmed§26-2C-2 (https://law.justia.com/codes/new-mexico/chapter-26/article-2c/section-26-2c-2/); NMOneSource re-check still requiredAs stated.
§1.5NMED measurement (20.10.2.7, final rule 28 Jan 2026): Total THC = delta-9 THC as measured using a post-decarboxylation method and based on percentage dry weight; THCA separately defined (CAS 23978-85-0)ConfirmedNMED final-rule PDF (https://www.env.nm.gov/cannabis-hemp/wp-content/uploads/sites/34/2025/12/20.10.2-NMAC-Final-Rule-1_28_2026.pdf), 20.10.2.7As stated.
§1.5Consequence: THCA counts toward Total THC after decarboxylation; a high-THCA flower exceeding 0.30% Total THC on that method is not compliant hemp, even if delta-9 THC alone is at or below 0.3%; this closes the THCA loophole at the manufacturing level in New Mexico. Repeated in the status table (high-THCA flower row); not duplicated there.Confirmed20.10.2.7 Total THC definition and 20.10.2.14(B)(1)(a) formula (final-rule PDF, same URL as above)As stated.
§1.5NMSU hemp guidance formula (delta-9 + 0.877 x THCA for LC) is consistent with post-decarboxylation accounting (secondary / university source), but the rule's own conversion formula, if any, must be quoted from 20.10.2 itself; do not present the NMSU formula as the ruleCorrected20.10.2.14(B)(1)(a) (final-rule PDF, same URL as above); NMSU guidance (https://arp.nmsu.edu/chapter-11/11-50.html)The rule itself states the formula at 20.10.2.14(B)(1)(a): Total THC = (0.877 x THCA) + THC. The NMSU formula matches the rule formula. The former instruction not to present the NMSU formula as the rule is superseded by the rule's own formula.

§1.5What the permanent rule does (NMED summary + Order, paraphrased): bans receipt, possession, manufacture, sale, advertising and marketing of semi-synthetic and synthetic cannabinoids at hemp facilities (extraction, manufacturing, warehouse and retail facilities operating in New Mexico, per NMED summary); named in secondary summaries: delta-8 THC (when chemically converted), delta-10 THC, THC-O, HHC, THCP and similar converted compoundsCorrected20.10.2.8(K) and 20.10.2.7(X) (final-rule PDF, same URL as above)20.10.2.8(K): a hemp facility shall not receive, possess, manufacture, offer, advertise, market, or sell semi-synthetic or synthetic cannabinoids or products containing them. Hemp facility (20.10.2.7(X)) means an extraction facility, manufacturing facility, retail manufacturer, or warehouse. The report's retail facilities summary wording is corrected to the rule's facility list.
§1.5Narrow exception: specific non-intoxicating semi-synthetic / synthetic cannabinoids (CBD, CBG, CBC, CBN in secondary summaries) may be used only if demonstrated by third-party testing to be at least 98% pure (Marijuana Herald / Harris Sliwoski); emergency rule noted to have accidentally duplicated the semi-synthetic definition instead of defining synthetic cannabinoid; whether the final rule corrects this is VerifyCorrected20.10.2.8(L) (final-rule PDF, same URL as above)20.10.2.8(L) exception: nine cannabinoids may be used as ingredients only if approved-laboratory analysis using a validated method shows purity at least 98%: (1) THCV, (2) CBC, (3) CBT (cannabicitran), (4) CBL, (5) CBE, (6) CBG, (7) CBDV, (8) CBD, (9) CBN. Whether the final rule fully corrects the emergency rule's duplicated semi-synthetic definition remains Verify on a full read of 20.10.2.7.
§1.5Limits Total THC in hemp finished products (NMED summary; numeric limits not stated on the Final Rule page)Corrected20.10.2.12 (final-rule PDF, same URL as above)20.10.2.12(A): finished products at or below 0.30% Total THC, at or below 2.0 mg Total THC per serving, at or below 20 mg per package; (B) tinctures at or below 100 mg per package; (C) broad-spectrum at or below 6.0 mg per package; (D) cosmetics and vapes exempt from (A)(2)–(3). §20.10.2.12(G) makes the §12 requirements effective 60 days after the part's effective date (60 days after 28 January 2026); §20.10.2.13(K) similarly delays certain labelling provisions 60 days.

Note (5): CCD's deferral policy and absence of CCD zoning rules rest on Vicente LLP analysis — Verify against CCD guidance (Part 3 route). The Estancia standalone-building requirement is a local rule, not a state rule.

3.6Local business licences: a state CCD licence is necessary but not sufficient where a locality requires its own licence, registration, permit or approval (examples: Albuquerque Retail Location Approval plus business licence; Santa Fe city permit; Las Cruces city permit; Rio Rancho city approvals/permits under ch. 122 before any business is conducted; Taos business registration before state licence application plus town cannabis-establishment permit; Las Vegas, NM business registration plus cannabis permit / zoning permit plus code inspections); local licences do not create a local cannabis tax; a local licence/permit revocation or expiry can have state consequences in Taos (town permit null and void if the state licence is revoked/expires, Ord. 25-04 s.6.K), while the converse is Verify; no locality in this file was found to impose a local cannabis licence cap (a numerical cap on how many local licences it will issue) - density is controlled by spacing and zoning, not by a cap number, in every ordinance excerpt readUnverifiedNo direct URL opened in audit - see follow-up route in Corrected wordingRetained. The no-cap finding is an absence finding across the excerpts read, not a code-wide proof. Follow-up: if a cap exists in an unopened code (for example Clovis, Alamogordo, Carlsbad, Raton, Torrance), it is Verify, and its compatibility with s.26-2C-12(B)(2) would need legal review.
3.7Buffer ceiling explanation: no locality may require more than 300 feet from a school/daycare in existence when the establishment was licensed (s.26-2C-12(B)(4)); every school/daycare buffer at or below 300 feet complies on its face; buffers from other uses (churches, residences, other retailers, tobacco retailers) are not subject to the 300-foot ceiling in the statute terms - which is why Rio Rancho (300 feet from churches/residences), Farmington (300 feet from religious institutions/other dispensaries) and Santa Fe city (300 feet from places of worship) can lawfully use 300-foot figures for those uses, and why Sandoval County 500-foot retailer/tobacco spacing is not on its face a (B)(4) violation; whether a non-school buffer is reasonable under (A)(1) is a separate, untested questionConfirmedhttps://law.justia.com/codes/new-mexico/chapter-26/article-2c/section-26-2c-12/Retained.

4.0.1s.26-2C-6(B) lists 12 items: (1) consumption areas, (2) couriers, (3) manufacturers, (4) producer microbusinesses, (5) producers, (6) research laboratories, (7) retailers, (8) servers, (9) testing laboratories, (10) training and education programs, (11) integrated cannabis microbusinesses, (12) vertically integrated cannabis establishments; the 10 CCD business licence types are producer, producer microbusiness, manufacturer, retailer, courier, testing laboratory, consumption area, research laboratory, ICMB and VICE, matching the RLD Apply for License page user guidesConfirmedhttps://law.justia.com/codes/new-mexico/chapter-26/article-2c/section-26-2c-6/Retained. History as shown on the mirror: Laws 2021 (1st S.S.) ch. 4 s.6; 2023 ch. 85 s.24; 2024 ch. 38 s.3.
4.0.2Universal rules: licence valid 12 months from issue, renewable annually (s.26-2C-6(E), 16.8.2.14(A)); clear designation for medical, commercial or both (s.26-2C-6(C)); non-transferable (s.26-2C-6(G), 16.8.2.8(N) - licence void and to be returned on location change, discontinuance, suspension or revocation unless an amended licence is obtained); 90-day decision clock on a completed application (s.26-2C-7(B), 16.8.2.8(G)); renewal window no earlier than 60 calendar days and no later than 30 days before expiration, with no sale/transfer/transport/manufacture/test/distribute until renewed if not timely renewed, and expiry at 11:59 p.m. on the expiration date (16.8.2.14(B)-(C)); tax gate on renewal - no delinquent CAN/GRT taxpayer status and no unfiled CAN/GRT returns (s.26-2C-6(F)); fees non-refundable (16.8.2.8(Q)); cash not accepted for fees (16.8.11.14 - credit/debit cards, electronic checks, electronic bank transfers, ACH, cashier checks); general application contents including controlling persons 21+, local-law compliance, TRD GRT registration, Secretary of State good standing, criminal-history screening (16.8.2.9) and the social and economic equity planConfirmedhttps://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title16/16.008.0002.htmlRetained. 16.8.2.14 was directly re-opened in the audit and confirms the 12-month period, the 60-to-30-day renewal window and the no-activity-until-renewed rule verbatim.
4.0.3No total-number cap on CCD licences was found in s.26-2C-6, 16.8.2 NMAC or on the RLD application page opened; s.26-2C-6(J) (the division shall not limit the number of licensed premises a licensee may occupy or operate) is a bar on limiting a licensee premises count, not by itself a statement that total licence numbers are uncapped; plant counts, by contrast, are capped; New Mexico regulates cultivation by mature-plant count, not by canopy (square-footage measurement in a cultivation plan under 16.8.2.27(B)(2) is a plan/diagram requirement, not a canopy cap)UnverifiedNo direct URL opened in audit - see follow-up route in Corrected wordingRetained phrased as no cap found in the law/rules opened, not as a CCD statement. The RLD social-equity page (reported to state that New Mexico does not place caps on the number of licences issued and has no lottery system) was not directly opened. Follow-up: open the RLD social-equity page or obtain a live CCD confirmation before asserting uncapped licence numbers unqualifiedly.
4.0.4Amended-licence application, fee and CCD approval required before implementing, among other things, an increase or decrease in plant count, a change in the licensee access to the water source or a 10% or more increase in water usage, or a material/substantial modification of the premises (16.8.2.23, producer); for consumption areas, 16.8.2.51 requires an amended application, fee and approval before a change of legal/business name, addition/elimination of a controlling person, or material/substantial premises modification, with CCD approval or denial within 90 days of a completed amended application; amendment fee $75 per amendment; designation of a non-controlling person as agent $75 per designation (16.8.11.10, as replaced 7 May 2024); VICE/ICMB applicants must request authority to add or remove an activity by amended application and any required additional fees and must not conduct an activity requiring additional authority until written division approval is received (16.8.2.8(Y)(3), (5))Confirmedhttps://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title16/16.008.0011.htmlRetained. 16.8.2.23 was directly re-opened in the audit (see the water row).
4.0.4Full cross-type amended-licence schedule (amended-licence procedure for each licence type beyond producer and consumption area)UnverifiedNo direct URL opened in audit - see follow-up route in Corrected wordingRetained Verify. Follow-up: each licence type amended-licence rule.
4.0.5Applications open as of October 2026: the RLD application page states CCD has implemented NM-PLUS, that applicants MUST submit online using NM-PLUS, that paper applications for initial licensure, amendments and renewals will no longer be accepted, lists user guides for all 10 business licence types and states no closed window, moratorium or suspension of new applications; a third-party page claiming research-laboratory applications were currently not open is not on an official page opened and is not adoptedUnverifiedhttps://www.rld.nm.gov/cannabis/licensing/new-applications/apply-for-license/Retained with a live-check caveat: NM-PLUS as the live route is established, but it does not prove every individual licence type accepted a submission on a given day in October 2026. Follow-up: live NM-PLUS login check per licence type on a specific date.
4.1Producer definition and scope (s.26-2C-2): cultivates cannabis plants; has unprocessed cannabis products tested by a testing laboratory; transports unprocessed cannabis products only to other cannabis establishments; sells cannabis products wholesale; licence required to cultivate except for personal use as provided by the Cannabis Regulation Act and LECUA (16.8.2.21(C)); no manufacture, courier or retail sale without the applicable licence type (16.8.2.21(D), except as provided in 16.8.2.8(BB))Confirmedhttps://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title16/16.008.0002.htmlRetained.
4.1Producer plant levels (16.8.8.9): Level 1: 201-2,000 mature cannabis plants; Level 2: 2,001-6,000; Level 3: 6,001-12,000; Level 4: 12,001-16,000; absolute maximum 20,000 mature cannabis plants at one time (16.8.8.9(F)); immature stages (germination, seedling, vegetative) excluded from the mature count (16.8.8.9(E)); mature cannabis plant means a female cannabis plant in the flowering stage (16.8.8.8(B)); the older 8,000-plant figure in the June 2023 CCD fee PDF and earlier/proposed tiers of 4,500 and 10,000 are supersededCorrectedhttps://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title16/16.008.0008.htmlLevel 1 lower bound RESOLVED at 201. The 401 figure was the 13 January 2022 emergency amendment only (NM Register Vol. XXXIII, Issue 2); the 22 March 2022 amendment (Vol. XXXIII, Issue 6) restored 201, and the current SRCA 16.8.8.9 text (opened in the audit, 1 November 2026) states 201-2,000. The 401 Verify flag is removed and the 401 figure must not be used as current law.
4.1Producer plant increases (16.8.8.9(C)-(D), 16.8.8.10(A), s.26-2C-9(C)): a licensee may increase mature plants at renewal and one other time per year, in increments of 500 mature plants, up to eight increments at a time upon application and approval; fees may be prorated for the remainder of the licensing yearCorrectedhttps://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title16/16.008.0008.htmlIncrement RESOLVED at 500. A 1,000-plant increment was reported for the 13 January 2022 emergency amendment only; the current SRCA 16.8.8.9(C) text (opened in the audit, 1 November 2026) states 500-plant increments, consistent with s.26-2C-9(C). The 1,000-increment Verify flag is removed. The flat $5.00/$2.50 per-plant rates are unaffected.
4.1Producer fees: $2,500 annually plus $1,000 per additional licensed premises, plus per-mature-plant fee $5.00 per commercial plant / $2.50 per medical-only plant (16.8.11.9(D), 16.8.11.11); worked example: a producer at 2,000 commercial plants = $2,500 base plus (2,000 x $5.00) = $12,500 before additional-premises fees; at 2,000 medical-only plants the plant fees are $5,000 plus the medical-only base fee (one-half); any source quoting $10 commercial / $5 medical per plant or an 8,000-plant cap is pre-2022 and must not be usedConfirmedhttps://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title16/16.008.0011.htmlRetained.
4.2Producer microbusiness: a producer at a single licensed premises possessing no more than 200 total mature cannabis plants at any one time (s.26-2C-2); no manufacture, retail or courier activity by itself; fee $1,000 annually flat (16.8.11.9(H), as amended 7 May 2024), no per-plant fee (16.8.11.11 expressly excepts producer microbusinesses); the old $500 (up to 100 plants) / $1,000 (101-200 plants) tier in the CCD fee PDF dated 12 June 2023 is superseded; anti-evasion rule s.26-2C-9(E) and 16.8.11.13 (a microbusiness or ICMB entering a business arrangement with another licensee with the purpose or effect of evading its licence limitations loses the lower fee and must pay the per-plant fee and, under the rule, the applicable producer or VICE fee); plant-count increases/decreases require an amended licence application (16.8.2.23(A)(3)-(4)); water condition applies to microbusinesses as well as producersConfirmedhttps://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title16/16.008.0011.htmlRetained.
4.3Manufacturer Classes I-IV (16.8.2.29(A)): Class I only packages/repackages or labels/relabels; Class II Class I activities plus edible/topical manufacture by infusion or other cannabis products other than extracts or concentrates, no extractions; Class III Class I and II plus extraction using mechanical methods or nonvolatile solvents; Class IV Class I, II and III plus extraction using volatile solvents or supercritical CO2; Class I manufacturers are exempt from the 16.8.6 health-and-safety facility requirements that Classes II-IV must follow for edible/topical finished products (CCD guidance, 23 March 2022, summarising 16.8.6.7(A)(2)); the class distinction is not a fee tier - manufacturer fee is flat $2,500 plus $1,000 per additional premises (16.8.11.9(C), s.26-2C-9(A)(3)); no plant or canopy limit on the manufacturer licence alone; other activities prohibited without the applicable licence (16.8.2.29(D), except 16.8.2.8(BB))Confirmedhttps://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/new-mexico/16-8-2-29-NMACRetained. Whether any operational class system beyond 16.8.2.29 exists remains a still-unverified sub-item (see the still-unverified list).
4.4Retailer: statutory definition (s.26-2C-2) a person that sells cannabis products to consumers; rule licence requirement (16.8.2.35(B)): no sale to qualified patients, primary caregivers, reciprocal participants or directly to consumers without a licence; no plant or canopy limit; fee $2,500 annually plus $1,000 per additional licensed premises (16.8.11.9(E), s.26-2C-9(A)(5)), subject to the consignment discountConfirmedhttps://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title16/16.008.0011.htmlRetained.
4.4Retailer consignment discount amount/percentage (s.26-2C-6(D): the division shall issue a licence to a cannabis retailer applicant at a discount if the applicant provides documentation of an agreement to accept cannabis products on consignment from a cannabis producer microbusiness or an integrated cannabis microbusiness)Unverifiedhttps://law.justia.com/codes/new-mexico/chapter-26/article-2c/section-26-2c-6/Retained Verify: the section states a discount but no figure. Do not quote a figure. Follow-up: s.26-2C-6(D) implementation / CCD guidance.
4.5Medical-only licences cost one-half (s.26-2C-9(D), repeated in 16.8.11.12): a medical-only retailer/producer/manufacturer/testing/research base fee is $1,250, not $2,500; VICE total cap $125,000 for both-activity licences (16.8.11.12, s.26-2C-9(D)) for application, licence, premises and plant fees and renewal equivalents; per-plant statutory ceiling $50 (s.26-2C-9(B), except producer microbusinesses and ICMBs) is a ceiling, not the charged rate - charged rates are $5.00 commercial / $2.50 medical-only (16.8.11.11); server-permit fee cap not more than $35 (s.26-2C-9(G))Confirmedhttps://law.justia.com/codes/new-mexico/chapter-26/article-2c/section-26-2c-9/Retained.
4.5 / 4.11Server-permit actual charged issuance fee; $10 replacement-permit figureUnverifiedhttps://law.justia.com/codes/new-mexico/chapter-26/article-2c/section-26-2c-9/Retained Verify. 4.6Proof of water - statute (s.26-2C-7(A)(3), as amended effective 1 July 2024 by Laws 2024, ch. 38): licensing of a cannabis producer or cannabis producer microbusiness is conditioned on demonstrating a legal right to a commercial water supply, water rights or other source of water sufficient to meet the water needs as determined by the division, evidenced by OSE documentation of a valid water right or water-provider documentation of compliance with provider rules; the 2024 amendment annotation clarifies the condition applies only to producers and producer microbusinesses; producers must additionally submit an energy/water-reduction plan (s.26-2C-7(A)(4): drip irrigation and water collection, natural lighting/energy efficiency, renewable energy)Confirmedhttps://law.justia.com/codes/new-mexico/chapter-26/article-2c/section-26-2c-7/Retained.
4.6Proof of water - rule and OSE practice (16.8.2.22(A)(5)): demonstration of a legal right to use the quantity of water the division determines is needed, evidenced by either (a) water-provider documentation of the right to use provider water and compliance with provider rules, or (b) OSE documentation of a valid and existing water right or a permit to develop a water right, for irrigation purposes for outdoor cultivation or a commercial purpose for indoor cultivation at the proposed place of use; acceptable OSE documentation includes (i) a state engineer permit or licence in good standing excluding a permit under ss.72-12-1, -1.1, -1.2 or -1.3 (domestic-well provisions), (ii) a subfile order or decree from a water-rights adjudication court, (iii) findings of an OSE hydrographic survey, or (iv) other documentation OSE has deemed in writing acceptable; application must also state initial mature/immature plant numbers and the amount of water planned monthly for a 12-month period (16.8.2.22(A)(11)); CCD producer checklist repeats the OSE list and requires an OSE Accession Form; OSE practice (OSE page and FAQ v.10, valid 10 July 2025): municipal water applicants do not go to OSE (RLD/CCD validates); privately owned rights are validated by OSE for correct configuration (outdoor = irrigation/agriculture, indoor = commercial); water rights must be in the applicant name or under a lease/user agreement supplied with the Accession Form, and a permit or change of ownership must be completed before submitting the Accession Form; short-term water hauling is a 1-year bridge only (hauler letter verifying a valid water right in sufficient amounts, contract for the amount required, documentation of the hauler own source, hauler must itself have legal access); a property purchase or an acequia share does not by itself carry a usable right - an OSE district-office check is requiredConfirmedhttps://www.ose.nm.gov/WR/cannabis.phpRetained. OSE Accession Form file: see the source list in the corrected file (RealFile OSE Accession Form, 12 June 2023).
4.6Water re-documentation trigger: 16.8.2.23 requires fresh water documentation on initial, amended or renewal licensure or on a 10% or more increase in water usage - stated in the original only from search snippets, with the full text of 16.8.2.23 not opened, so not to be stated as settledCorrectedhttps://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title16/16.008.0002.htmlTrigger CONFIRMED on the full rule text, opened in the audit (1 November 2026): a producer must obtain division approval of an amended licence before implementing a change of water source or of its water and energy conservation plan (16.8.2.23(A)(2)), and a change in the licensee access to the water source submitted with an application for initial, amended, or renewal licensure, or a 10% or more increase in water usage, is a material or substantial change (16.8.2.23(D)(3)). The snippet-only Verify flag is removed.
4.6VICE/ICMB water: a VICE or ICMB applicant must meet all qualifications for each establishment type authorised (16.8.2.8(Y)(1)), so the production limb of a VICE/ICMB application carries the same water demonstration in practiceUnverifiedNo direct URL opened in audit - see follow-up route in Corrected wordingRetained Verify on the application forms. Follow-up: VICE/ICMB application forms via CCD for the water item before stating it as a separate VICE/ICMB condition.
4.6Water enforcement: failure to meet the Act/rules is a ground for denial (s.26-2C-7(C): the division shall deny an initial licence or renewal application if it does not include information required by the division or the applicant does not meet the requirements of the Act or rules); the division may refuse, suspend or revoke under the Uniform Licensing Act for non-compliance (s.26-2C-7(D)); a specific OSE/CCD water enforcement action with a date and outcomeUnverifiedhttps://law.justia.com/codes/new-mexico/chapter-26/article-2c/section-26-2c-7/Grounds retained as stated. No specific dated water enforcement action (denial, revocation or other outcome) was verified in the audit. Follow-up: CCD disciplinary / denial records and OSE cannabis enforcement records.
4.7Social equity - what officially exists: statutory duty s.26-2C-3(B)(7)-(10) (procedures promoting participation by representatives of communities disproportionately harmed by cannabis-arrest enforcement, rural communities likely to be impacted by cannabis production and agricultural producers from economically disadvantaged communities; procedures promoting racial, ethnic, gender and geographic diversity and New Mexico residency; certification for products from ICMBs/producer microbusinesses or businesses owned by representatives of those communities and underserved communities including tribal, acequia, land grant-merced and other rural historic communities; technical-assistance resource guide for rural residents); required social and economic equity plan in every application (for example 16.8.2.22(A)(19) producer, same item in 16.8.2.57 research laboratory, and CCD checklists); annual demographic collection and publication s.26-2C-3(F) (applicants, controlling persons, employees: race, ethnicity, gender, age, residential status, underserved-rural location; presented to the legislature interim committee); low-barrier design as the equity mechanism (microbusiness/ICMB structure, $5.00/$2.50 plant rates, retailer consignment discount); and the negative finding that there is NO standalone social-equity licence, lottery, set-aside or fee waiver found in the statute or rules readConfirmedhttps://law.justia.com/codes/new-mexico/chapter-26/article-2c/section-26-2c-3/Retained, including the explicit negative finding (no programme invented). The RLD social-equity page substance on plant rates matches current 16.8.11.11 even though the page itself was not opened.

4.8LECUA medical conversion as legacy-continuation plus relicensing, not an automatic conversion into an adult-use licence and not a new competitive round for incumbents: priority processing from 1 September 2021 for producers/microbusinesses and LECUA licensees in good standing (s.26-2C-7(A)(1)), other types by 1 January 2022 (s.26-2C-7(A)(2)); continued operation under the LECUA licence until comparable commercial licences were available (s.26-2C-6(M)), retail commercial sales to begin no later than 1 April 2022 (in fact 1 April 2022), medical activity continuing under medical-programme rules until CCD promulgated medical-activity rules; rule mechanism 16.8.2.8(W): a person properly licensed and in good standing under LECUA on 29 June 2021 must submit a completed renewal application for a cannabis establishment licence with required fees within 30 days of the division notifying the licensee that a renewal application is available, else cease all production operations immediately, and on approval operates under the Cannabis Regulation Act/CCD rules, continuing under Department of Health medical rules only where they do not conflict; designation plus one-half medical-only fee on conversion; corporate-form conversion for legacy medical nonprofits under s.26-2C-6(Q) (added by Laws 2024, ch. 38, effective 1 July 2024) into a Business Corporation Act corporation, LLC, limited partnership or partnership on filing restated articles / articles of organisation / certificate / statement with the secretary of state; no separate conversion fee, conversion application form or automatic adult-use entitlement foundConfirmedhttps://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title16/16.008.0002.htmlRetained. 16.8.2.8(W) was confirmed on the SRCA 16.8.2 page opened in the audit. No CCD conversion guidance document was opened - that operational-checklist gap is noted in the still-unverified list.
4.9.1Courier (16.8.2.41): licence required to transport cannabis products directly to qualified patients (at least 18), primary caregivers, reciprocal participants or directly to consumers (at least 21); deliveries only from a retail licensee with which the courier is employed or has a disclosed delivery agreement (16.8.2.41(D)(1)-(2)); only shelf-stable products may be delivered, perishable / time-and-temperature-controlled products may not (D)(9); a delivery package may not be held longer than 24 hours (D)(7); delivery vehicles must not advertise cannabis transport (D)(8); vehicle value cap $10,000 with each product associated with a specific order (F); per-consumer delivery cap: more than two ounces of cannabis, 16 grams of cannabis extract and 800 milligrams of edible cannabis prohibited (I)(3); no plant/canopy limit; fee $250 annually plus $100 per additional licensed premises (16.8.11.9(A); statute s.26-2C-9(A)(1) allows up to $1,500 plus up to $1,000 per additional premises, the rule amount is operative); application/renewal contents at 16.8.2.42 including vehicle registration/insurance and a delivery planConfirmedhttps://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title16/16.008.0011.htmlRetained.
4.9.2Testing laboratory: definition (s.26-2C-2) a facility that samples, collects and tests cannabis products and transports cannabis products for the purpose of testing; testing categories (16.8.2.43(A)): visual inspection, microbiological, residual solvents, potency and homogeneity, heavy metals, pesticides, and such other categories as the department may identify; ownership bar (16.8.2.43(D)): no person with a direct or indirect interest in any cannabis establishment other than a cannabis research laboratory may hold an interest in a cannabis testing laboratory; and s.26-2C-6(G): the division shall not allow a person licensed as any type of cannabis establishment other than a cannabis research laboratory to hold, directly or indirectly, a cannabis testing laboratory licence; internal quality-control testing by an establishment using validated methods, without offering testing services to others, does not require a testing-lab licence (16.8.2.43(B)); no plant/canopy limit; fee $2,500 plus $1,000 per additional premises (16.8.11.9(B); statute allows up to $2,500); renewal includes an annual continuing demonstration of capability (CDC) for each test (16.8.2.44(C): ISO/IEC 17025 scope evidence, proficiency testing, or re-performance of the initial demonstration of capability)Confirmedhttps://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title16/16.008.0002.htmlRetained.
4.9.3Consumption area Types I and II (16.8.2.49(A)): Type I - cannabis products may be consumed on the licensed premises except products consumed through the respiratory system; Type II - including products consumed through the respiratory system (the rule own wording calls these permits within the consumption-area licence; the s.26-2C-6(B)(1) item is cannabis consumption areas); retailer-qualification prerequisite (16.8.2.49(E)): applicants must meet all qualifications for a cannabis retailer; general consumption bar (16.8.2.8(D)): licensees shall prohibit consumption on or within the licensed premises unless a cannabis consumption area has been approved; smoking restriction: smoking in a consumption area only in a designated smoking area or a standalone building from which smoke does not infiltrate other indoor workplaces/public places where smoking is otherwise prohibited under the Dee Johnson Clean Indoor Air Act (16.8.2.55, s.26-2C-6(K)); server-permit link: all employees who directly offer, sell or serve cannabis in a consumption area must hold a current cannabis server permit (16.8.2.54(F), citing 16.8.10 NMAC); no plant/canopy limit; fee $2,500 annually (16.8.11.9(J); statute allows up to $2,500); a secondary claim of a $2,500/$5,000 Type I/Type II fee split was not adopted - the official rule states a single $2,500 feeConfirmedhttps://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title16/16.008.0011.htmlRetained.
4.9.3Consumption-area additional-premises fee treatmentUnverifiedhttps://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title16/16.008.0011.htmlRetained Verify: 16.8.11.9(J) as read lists no additional-premises line for this type. Follow-up: SRCA 16.8.11.9(J) / CCD.
4.9.4Research laboratory Tiers I-III (16.8.2.56(A)): Tier I may produce cannabis to be ingested by human or animal subjects, or produce cannabis not meant for ingestion, for division-approved clinical, agricultural or market research studies, produce federally legal cannabis products, and conduct division-approved studies; Tier II may produce cannabis not meant for ingestion, or purchase cannabis to be ingested by human or animal subjects, for division-approved studies, and conduct division-approved studies; Tier III may not produce cannabis and may only purchase cannabis or cannabis products from licensed Tier I and Tier II laboratories as appropriate for approved studies, and may conduct clinical, agricultural or market research studies; general research authority (16.8.2.56(C)): except as noted in subsection B, a research laboratory licence permits production, processing, transport, transfer, sale and possession consistent with its licence type for research and related purposes; Tier II/III purchase from another licensed establishment requires division approval and is limited to brand-specific/cultivar-specific inquiries where research-lab product is impossible (16.8.2.56(B)); fee $2,500 plus $1,000 per additional premises (16.8.11.9(F)); application/renewal contents at 16.8.2.57 including tier sought, research plan and any DEA licence/conditional approval or plan to seek itConfirmedhttps://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title16/16.008.0002.htmlRetained.
4.9.4Research-laboratory plant-count limitUnverifiedhttps://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title16/16.008.0002.htmlRetained Verify: no plant-count limit for research laboratories was stated in 16.8.2.56 as opened. Production is tied to division-approved studies, not to the 16.8.8 producer tiers (which by their terms apply to producer and VICE licences). Do not apply the 200 / 20,000 figures to research labs. Follow-up: full 16.8.2.56 NMAC plus CCD research-lab guidance.
4.9.5ICMB (s.26-2C-2): a person licensed to conduct one or more of (1) production of cannabis at a single licensed premises, provided the person shall not possess more than 200 total mature cannabis plants at any one time, (2) manufacture of cannabis products at a single licensed premises, (3) sales and transportation of cannabis products produced or manufactured by that person or another cannabis producer microbusiness or integrated cannabis microbusiness, (4) operation of only one retail establishment, and (5) couriering of cannabis products to consumers; rule application route 16.8.2.8(Y)(1)-(2): applicants must meet all qualifications for each type authorised, apply for authorisation for one or more of production, manufacturing, retail establishment or courier, request authority to add or remove an activity by amended application and any required additional fees, and not conduct an activity requiring additional authority until written division approval; fee $2,500 annually flat (16.8.11.9(I), as amended 7 May 2024), no per-plant fee (16.8.11.11); the old $1,000 (2 activities) / $1,500 (3) / $2,000 (4) / $2,500 (5) tier in the 2023 CCD PDF is superseded; evasion rule as in s.4.2Confirmedhttps://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title16/16.008.0011.htmlRetained.
4.9.5ICMB additional-premises fee in the rule text (statute allows an additional $500 per licensed premises, s.26-2C-9(A)(9); rule text in 16.8.11.9(I) as read lists no additional-premises amount)Unverifiedhttps://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title16/16.008.0011.htmlRetained Verify. 4.9.6VICE (s.26-2C-2): a person authorised to act as one or more of (1) a cannabis courier, (2) a cannabis manufacturer, (3) a cannabis producer, and (4) a cannabis retailer; application route the same 16.8.2.8(Y) text as ICMB; if not all activity is on a single premises, each additional premises requires an additional premises fee (16.8.2.8(Y)(4)); plant limits the same producer tiers as a standalone producer - 16.8.8.9(A) expressly covers all cannabis producer and VICE licences issued on or after 15 August 2021: Level 1: 201-2,000; Level 2: 2,001-6,000; Level 3: 6,001-12,000; Level 4: 12,001-16,000; absolute maximum 20,000 mature cannabis plants at one time (16.8.8.9(F)); increases in 500-plant increments, up to eight increments at a time, at renewal and once more per year (16.8.8.9(C)-(D)); no canopy limit; fee $7,500 annually plus $1,000 per additional licensed premises, plus per-plant fees ($5.00 commercial / $2.50 medical), subject to the $125,000 total cap for both-activity licences (16.8.11.9(G), 16.8.11.12, s.26-2C-9(D)); medical-only VICE fees one-halfCorrectedhttps://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title16/16.008.0008.htmlVICE plant figures now stated without the 401 lower-bound and 1,000-increment Verify qualifiers that appeared in the original s.4.9.6 text. The qualifiers are removed because the current SRCA 16.8.8.9 text (opened in the audit, 1 November 2026) confirms 201-2,000 and 500-plant increments (see the s.4.1 rows).
4.10Summary fee table (current rule fees, 16.8.11 NMAC as amended 7 May 2024): all fees annual for issuance or renewal, all licensing/renewal fees non-refundable (16.8.2.8(Q)); medical-only base fees one-half the both-activity fee except where a type has no medical/commercial distinction in the fee rule; producer $2,500 plus per-plant fees, plus $1,000 per additional premises; microbusiness $1,000 flat, single premises; manufacturer (Classes I-IV) $2,500 plus $1,000; retailer $2,500 (before any consignment discount - amount Verify) plus $1,000; courier $250 plus $100; testing laboratory $2,500 plus $1,000; consumption area (Type I/II) $2,500, additional premises not stated in 16.8.11.9(J) - Verify; research laboratory (Tier I/II/III) $2,500 plus $1,000; ICMB $2,500 flat, statute allows plus $500 per additional premises, rule text silent - Verify; VICE $7,500 plus per-plant fees, total capped at $125,000 (both-activity), plus $1,000; other administrative fees: licence amendment $75 per amendment, designation of a non-controlling person as agent $75 per designation (16.8.11.10); statutory fee caps that are not the charged fee: courier up to $1,500 (charged $250), testing laboratory up to $2,500 (charged $2,500), producer microbusiness up to $1,000 (charged $1,000), ICMB up to $2,500 (charged $2,500), consumption area up to $2,500 (charged $2,500), per-plant ceiling $50 (charged $5.00/$2.50); superseded figures that must not be used: producer per-plant $10 commercial / $5 medical (pre-January 2022), plant caps of 4,500 / 8,000 / 10,000 (pre-2022 tiers), producer-microbusiness $500/$1,000 by plant count and ICMB $1,000/$1,500/$2,000/$2,500 by activity count (CCD fee PDF dated 12 June 2023, superseded by the 7 May 2024 amendment to 16.8.11.9), training-and-education as a fee-bearing licence (superseded 1 July 2024)Confirmedhttps://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title16/16.008.0011.htmlRetained, subject to the three Verify items carried in the table itself (retailer consignment discount amount, consumption-area additional-premises treatment, ICMB additional-premises treatment in the rule text).
4.11Server permit (NOT a business licence; included because s.26-2C-6(B)(8) lists it): an individual to be employed as a server - directly offering, selling or serving cannabis - in a licensed cannabis consumption area; it does not authorise operating a business; statute s.26-2C-11(B), (E): the division shall issue cannabis server permits to persons 21 years of age or older who satisfy the requirements of the section and division rules, on proof of satisfactory completion of a programme provided by a cannabis server permit education provider approved by the division; a person shall not be employed as a cannabis server on a licensed premises unless that person obtains a cannabis server permit within 30 days of employment; permits valid 3 years from issue and renewable on proof of successful completion of up to 4.5 hours of continuing education and an examination as determined by the division; rule detail 16.8.10.8(A)-(B) (N, 07/12/2022): a server must complete a programme every 3 years, satisfactory completion requires a score of 80% or higher on an approved test, a person not previously certified must obtain a permit within 30 days of employment; a cannabis research laboratory or its employee is not required to obtain or possess a server permit while performing activities authorised under a research laboratory licence (s.26-2C-11(A)); server permits are issued via approved education providers, not via the NM-PLUS business-licence guides; no closure was foundConfirmedhttps://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title16/16.008.0010.pdfRetained. Issuance fee and provider list remain Verify (see the s.4.5/s.4.11 fee row and the still-unverified list).
4.12Training and education programme (REGISTRATION ONLY, not a licence; included because s.26-2C-6(B)(10) lists it): current law s.26-2C-10 (repealed and reenacted by Laws 2024, ch. 38, s.6, effective 1 July 2024): a New Mexico public post-secondary educational institution may offer a practical or academic curriculum designed to prepare students for participation in the cannabis industry; the institution shall register its cannabis training and education program with the division, which shall include the information about the program on its website; do not present cannabis training and education as an 11th CCD business licence type in October 2026; pre-July-2024 material describing it as a licence is superseded; it is open only to New Mexico public post-secondary institutions, it is registration (not licensure), and the 12-month licence validity / 60-to-30-day renewal window for business licences does not apply to it on the face of s.26-2C-10; no fee, plant limit or cap applies; no registration window/closure was found in s.26-2C-10Confirmedhttps://law.justia.com/codes/new-mexico/chapter-26/article-2c/section-26-2c-10/Retained. The CCD programme list itself was not directly opened - see the still-unverified list.
4.13Other CCD authorisations: no separate cannabis nursery CCD licence was found in s.26-2C-6(B) or 16.8.2 NMAC as opened; a 2023 bill (HB 313, 56th Legislature, 1st Session) proposed creating a cannabis nursery licence and raising microbusiness plant counts to 1,000 - proposed only, not current law; no separate CCD distributor, transporter (other than courier) or wholesaler licence was found (wholesale movement is within producer/manufacturer/VICE authority; consumer delivery is courier authority); personal production (home grow) is not a CCD business licence (16.8.2.21(C) excepts personal use as provided by the Cannabis Regulation Act and LECUA); patient personal-production rules belong to Part 1/Part 11 scopeConfirmedhttps://law.justia.com/codes/new-mexico/chapter-26/article-2c/section-26-2c-6/Retained.
4.14Hemp summary - who does what and plan status: the Hemp Manufacturing Act is NMSA 1978, ss.76-24-1 et seq., not ss.26-2C-x (NMED rule: Act means the Hemp Manufacturing Act, Section 76-24-1, et seq., NMSA 1978); NMDA issues licences to businesses/individuals cultivating hemp; NMED issues permits to businesses/individuals for processing activities following harvest, including extraction, distillation and manufacturing; there is no NMDA processor licence - post-harvest processing is NMED-only; USDA plan status is New Mexico own USDA-approved state plan, NOT USDA-direct: USDA AMS List of USDA-approved Hemp Plans (page stated Updated February 17, 2026) lists New Mexico as an approved plan under the final rule effective 22 March 2021, and the NMDA Hemp Program page states that as of 1 January 2022 New Mexico began operating under a USDA-approved state plan administered by NMDAConfirmedhttps://nmdeptag.nmsu.edu/licensing-and-registrations/hemp-registration.htmlRetained. USDA plan page: https://www.ams.usda.gov/rules-regulations/hemp/state-and-tribal-plan-review
4.14.1NMDA Annual Hemp Commercial (Research) Production Licence - field / annual crop: planting an annual hemp crop in the field only, not intended for growers maintaining viable hemp plants throughout the year as part of a greenhouse or plant nursery operation; term: licence expires 240 days after date of issuance, harvest within the 240-day period; 21.20.2.7(A): Annual Production License means a licence issued for the production of a single crop that is destroyed within 240 days of planting; application timing 21.20.2.8(A): apply no less than 25 business days prior to planting of each crop at each location, separate application and fee for each new crop at each location; area rule (2026 form): no acreage limit for a single contiguous growing area, multiple non-contiguous areas on one licence only if within a 2.5-mile radius, total under 10 acres, and all planted within a 3-week period, landowner affidavit required if the applicant does not own the land; fees current (2026 form, Updated January 2026): base registration/inspection fee $650.00 plus $6.00 per acre (minimum $6.00) plus $10.00 per variety (minimum $10.00), refunds not available or transferable once payment is processedConfirmedhttps://nmdeptag.nmsu.edu/media/pdf/annual-hemp-commercial-production-application.pdfRetained as the current charged fees.
4.14.1NMDA Continuous Hemp Commercial (Research) Production Licence - indoor / greenhouse / nursery, year-round: maintaining viable hemp plants throughout the year as part of a greenhouse or plant nursery operation (including clonal production), not intended for production of an annual crop; term: licence valid from 1 February 2026 through 31 January 2027; 21.20.2.7(F) and 21.20.2.8(B): a continuous licence expires 31 January of each year and renewal must be applied for prior to 1 February; area rule (2026 form): no limit for a single contiguous growing area, multiple non-contiguous areas on one licence only if within a 2.5-mile radius and total under 10 acres / 435,600 sq ft; fees current (2026 form, Updated January 2026): base registration/inspection fee $750.00 plus $0.75 per 1,000 square feet (minimum $5.00) plus $10.00 per variety (minimum $10.00)Confirmedhttps://nmdeptag.nmsu.edu/media/pdf/continuous-hemp-commercial-application.pdfRetained as the current charged fees.
4.14.1NMDA common requirements (both grower licences, 2026 forms plus 21.20.2.9 NMAC): criminal background check required; hemp commercial production licences cannot be issued to individuals with felony convictions related to controlled substances within the last 10 years; applicant must supply the state Department of Public Safety report/stamp ($15.00 DPS charge stated in the form); compliance with the New Mexico Child Support Enforcement Act - failure can result in denial/revocation; licence non-transferable (may not be reassigned/transferred to another business, location, individual or entity); harvest only with NMDA-issued documents authorising harvest of the specific varieties listed; field inspections and plant samples within 30 days of the estimated harvest date; licensee responsible for delivery of samples to an NMDA-approved laboratory for THC determination (post-decarboxylation) before harvest and for destruction/disposition costs of non-compliant (over 0.3% THC) varieties; Harvest Notification Document submitted no less than 30 days prior to estimated harvest date; Hemp Harvest Certificate certifying a quantity of hemp meets the THC concentration required - NMED facilities may only accept New Mexico hemp with a PASS harvest certificate plus a transportation manifest; licence is proof of state registration as a hemp producer and is required by law enforcement if you have viable hemp plants or are a grower in possession of raw hempConfirmedhttps://nmdeptag.nmsu.edu/licensing-and-registrations/hemp-registration.htmlRetained.
4.14.1Rule-vs-form variance: the still-posted 21.20.2.10 NMAC text (dated 11 December 2018) states higher caps - $800 per location for annual, $900 for continuous, and $25 per variety in excess of one - while the 2026 NMDA forms charge $650/$750 and $10 per variety; use the 2026 form figures as the current charged fees and note the 2018 rule text has not been updated on the SRCA posting; do not present $800/$900 as the 2026 feeUnverifiedhttps://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title21/21.020.0002.htmlRetained as a variance flag for Part 7. Follow-up: confirm whether 21.20.2 NMAC has been amended by a later instrument not reflected on the SRCA page, or whether NMDA is charging under plan/policy authority. Part 7 must not silently reconcile these.
4.14.2NMED post-harvest permits (20.10.2 NMAC, repealed-and-replaced effective 28 January 2026, making permanent the 1 August 2025 emergency amendment; 20.10.2.5 effective date 28 January 2026 unless a later date is cited at the end of a section): statutory authority 20.10.2.3 (Section 76-24-8 NMSA 1978 authorises the environment department to issue permits to extract, process or engage in other manufacturing activities regarding hemp and directs the department to adopt permitting rules that include fees); objective 20.10.2.6 (uniform standards for transportation, extraction, processing and testing of hemp products for safe manufacture and accurate presentation for human consumption, absorption and inhalation); scope 20.10.2.2 (all individuals, businesses, agencies, institutions or other entities engaged in transportation, extraction, storage or processing of hemp products in New Mexico); s.76-24-8: the department of environment shall issue permits pursuant to rules under Subsection C to extract, process or engage in other manufacturing activities regarding hemp, including manufacturing intermediate hemp-derived products and hemp finished products, and a person shall not do so without a permit from the department of environment or a licence under Subsection C of Section 76-24-10; fees not to exceed the lesser of $1,000 or the cost of administration of a permit; history Laws 2019, ch. 116, s.6; 2020, ch. 32, s.6Confirmedhttps://www.env.nm.gov/cannabis-hemp/wp-content/uploads/sites/34/2025/12/20.10.2-NMAC-Final-Rule-1_28_2026.pdfRetained. Final-rule hub: https://www.env.nm.gov/cannabis-hemp/hemp-final-rule/
4.14.2NMED four current permit types, verbatim definitions (20.10.2.7) and fees (20.10.2.8(D)(1)): Hemp Extraction Facility (an operation that produces hemp extract - hemp extract means oil and extracts derived from hemp, containing THC in any concentration, including cannabidiol, cannabidiolic acid and other identified and non-identified compounds) $1,000; Hemp Manufacturing Facility (an operation, other than a hemp extraction facility, hemp retail manufacturer or hemp warehouse that produces or repackages hemp products, other than hemp extract, and provides hemp products for sale or distribution to other business entities - i.e. wholesale manufacturing) $1,000; Hemp Warehouse (a location, other than a hemp extraction facility, hemp manufacturing facility or hemp retail manufacturer where hemp extract is stored) $1,000; Hemp Retail Manufacturer (NEW in the 28 Jan 2026 rule, replacing the former Hemp Processing Facility type: an operation that produces or repackages hemp finished products and provides them directly to consumers; NMED final-rule summary: retail producers such as restaurants and bakeries meet the same requirements as wholesale producers; special limit: unless approved, a hemp retail manufacturer shall only receive and use hemp extract that is broad spectrum (20.10.2.8(C)(6)) - broad spectrum means THC removed, at most 0.005% total THC (20.10.2.7(H))) $500; other NMED fees (20.10.2.8(D)): late renewal fee $200 if renewal application plus fee are not received on or before the permit expiration date, re-inspection fee $500 (payable before the re-inspection or before renewal approval), variance application fee $300, the regulatory authority may also charge administrative compliance costs, all fees non-refundableConfirmedhttps://www.env.nm.gov/cannabis-hemp/wp-content/uploads/sites/34/2025/12/20.10.2-NMAC-Final-Rule-1_28_2026.pdfRetained.
4.14.2NMED permit mechanics (20.10.2.8): a person may not operate a hemp facility without a valid permit to operate issued by the regulatory authority (A)(1); when more than a single hemp facility is operated on the premises, each one shall be separately permitted (A)(2) - so an operation that both extracts and then formulates finished product needs two permits (extraction plus manufacturing); exception: a hemp facility permitted as a hemp manufacturing facility, hemp extraction facility or hemp retail manufacturer is not required to also be permitted as a hemp warehouse (A)(9); permits non-transferable from one person to another, from one location to another, or from one type of operation to another (E)(5); permits expire on the last day of the anniversary month of the date of original issue (D)(3); application at least 30 calendar days before operating, constructing, converting, remodelling/changing facility type, or opening/changing ownership (B)(1); issuance requires a completed application, fee, approval and a pre-operational inspection; each facility must file a written operational plan plus per-product information (ingredients by weight, pH, water activity, full procedure including extraction method and solvent removal, packaging, label, batch/lot coding, shelf-life, distribution); manufacturing employees must hold a valid food handler card (within 30 days of employment if not held at hire; card valid 3 years; requirement effective 60 days after the rule effective date) (20.10.2.9(H)); transport only to NMED-permitted facilities or persons approved by the regulatory authority, under a hemp transportation manifest (20.10.2.10); testing (20.10.2.14): every batch/lot of finished product for human consumption, cosmetics or inhalation must be tested by an NMED-approved analytical laboratory before it leaves the facility - cannabinoid profile (Total THC = 0.877 x THCA + THC, delta-9-THC, THCA, CBD, CBDA), label-content verification, solvents and pesticide profile as determined by NMEDConfirmedhttps://www.env.nm.gov/cannabis-hemp/wp-content/uploads/sites/34/2025/12/20.10.2-NMAC-Final-Rule-1_28_2026.pdfRetained.
4.14.2NMED permit-required trigger (NMED FAQ, opened 31 October 2026): a permit from NMED is required when manufacturing hemp-containing products for human ingestion, absorption or smokable products; a hemp manufacturing permit from NMED is required for drying and/or processing (i.e. trimming) of hemp/hemp flower into a finished product or product that does not need further processing to be offered as a finished product; the FAQ blanket statement that a non-refundable fee of $1,000 is required with each hemp application predates the $500 retail-manufacturer distinction - use the rule $500 retail figure, not the FAQ blanket $1,000; the FAQ also still defines hemp facility as extraction/manufacturing/warehouse only (omitting retail manufacturer) - where FAQ and 20.10.2 NMAC conflict, the rule governsConfirmedhttps://www.env.nm.gov/cannabis-hemp/hemp-final-rule/Retained.
4.14.2NMED finished-product THC limits (20.10.2.12, effective 60 days after 28 January 2026): unless otherwise specified, a hemp finished product shall (1) not exceed 0.30% total THC concentration, (2) contain no more than 2.0 mg total THC per serving, and (3) no more than 20 mg total THC per package; exceptions: hemp tinctures at most 100 mg total THC per package; broad-spectrum finished products at most 6.0 mg total THC per package; cosmetics and vapes are exempt from the per-serving/per-package mg limits (but not from the 0.30% concentration limit as written in s.12(A)(1) - flag this nuance rather than stating vapes/cosmetics are uncapped); synthetic / semi-synthetic cannabinoids (20.10.2.11(K)-(L)): as a general rule a hemp facility shall not receive, possess, manufacture, offer, advertise, market or sell semisynthetic cannabinoids or synthetic cannabinoids or products containing them; narrow exception: the nine listed cannabinoids - THCV, CBC, CBT, CBL, CBE, CBG, CBDV, CBD, CBN - may be received/used as ingredients only if approved-lab analysis by a validated method shows at least 98% purity before use; delta-8, delta-10, THC-O and HHC are not on the nine-item exception list and therefore fall under the general prohibition as written - but Part 7 should quote 20.10.2.11(K)-(L) rather than naming a product-by-product ban list, since the rule works by exception list; this is the current (28 January 2026) position and supersedes looser summaries of the August 2025 emergency ruleConfirmedhttps://www.env.nm.gov/cannabis-hemp/wp-content/uploads/sites/34/2025/12/20.10.2-NMAC-Final-Rule-1_28_2026.pdfRetained as originally sourced to 20.10.2 NMAC. These two subsections were not re-opened line-by-line in the audit and are carried forward on the original sourcing; a line-by-line re-check against the final rule PDF is a Part 7 follow-up, not a reason to downgrade the rule citation.
4.14.2Hemp-derived product registration / retailer rule - what exists and what does not: no separate hemp-derived product registration was found on any official NMDA or NMED source opened (products are controlled through the facility permit plus per-product operational-plan information plus batch/lot testing plus labelling (20.10.2.12-.14), not through a standalone product-registration licence; do not invent a product-registration fee or number); no retailer licence/permit: NMED FAQ verbatim - Do I need a permit to sell pre-packaged CBD or other hemp products? No, not at this time (NMED recommends verifying that pre-packaged product comes from a properly permitted/licensed manufacturer); Hemp Retailer is defined in 20.10.2.7(FF) (a person that provides hemp finished products directly to consumers) but it is not a permit type - the permit type for direct-to-consumer production is Hemp Retail Manufacturer; a pure reseller of pre-packaged product needs no NMED permit as of 31 October 2026Confirmedhttps://www.env.nm.gov/cannabis-hemp/wp-content/uploads/sites/34/2025/12/20.10.2-NMAC-Final-Rule-1_28_2026.pdfRetained as a negative finding (none found on official sources opened).
4.14.3Other NMDA licences under 21.20.3 NMAC (Hemp Manufacturing Rule - name is misleading): despite its title, 21.20.3 does NOT license NMED post-harvest manufacturing; its scope (21.20.3.2) is only (A) testing of raw hemp for regulatory purposes as identified by NMDA, and (B) plant breeding involving viable plants over 0.3% and under 5% THC; Laboratory Hemp Testing Licence (21.20.3.11): persons testing raw hemp for the purpose of supporting regulatory requirements established by the department - i.e. THC quantification supporting a Hemp Harvest Certificate; requires demonstrated analytical proficiency, department-approved SOPs, lab-director credentials and proficiency-test participation (max 2 per 12 months if satisfactory); fee in rule text shall not exceed $500 per year (21.20.3.9(A)), double fee if late; licence year 1 Feb-31 Jan, expires 31 Jan following issuance (21.20.3.8); Special Hemp Breeding Licence (21.20.3.12): persons breeding for new or improved varieties of hemp and that may possess viable plants or plant material in excess of 0.3% and less than 5% THC shall be licensed by NMDA; over 0.3%-under 5% material must be kept indoors in a department-approved secure area, must not be available to the public or transferred to anyone without a valid Special Hemp Breeding Licence, and must not be used for any purpose other than plant breeding; law enforcement is notified of licensed locations; fee in rule text shall not exceed $500 per year (21.20.3.9(B)), double fee if late, director may waive fees in special circumstances (21.20.3.9(E)); licence year 1 Feb-31 Jan; Hemp Nursery Plant Licence (listed on the NMDA Hemp Registration page): required by state law for any business selling live plants, including hemp (Continuous form adds: including hemp clones); this is a general nursery licence applied to hemp sellers, not a separate hemp-cultivation licence; citation trap: NMED 20.10.2.7(Z) defines hemp harvest certificate as certifying THC pursuant to 21.20.3 NMAC and NMED FAQ repeats 21.20.3, while the cultivation/THC rule itself is 21.20.2 NMAC and 21.20.3 is the lab/breeding rule that defines the harvest-certificate document (21.20.3.7(E)) - Part 7 should cite 21.20.2 for cultivation and 21.20.3 for lab/breeding and note NMED cross-reference as writtenConfirmedhttps://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title21/21.020.0003.htmlRetained for rule scope and rule caps. Actual 2026 form fees and the Nursery Plant Licence fee/term are separately Verify (next row).
4.14.3NMDA Nursery Plant Licence fee and term; actual 2026 charged fees for the NMDA Laboratory Hemp Testing and Special Hemp Breeding licences (rule caps are at most $500; the 2026 application forms for these two licences were not opened)Unverifiedhttps://nmdeptag.nmsu.edu/licensing-and-registrations/hemp-registration.htmlRetained Verify. 4.14.4CCD interaction - what can be stated on official sources: no official source opened states that intoxicating hemp products require a CCD licence; the position that can be stated runs the other way - NMED Hemp Rule FAQ, Q8 (official, opened 31 October 2026), verbatim question: I make cannabis products that include hemp ingredients under my CCD license, do I need any type of permit from CHB? - Yes. You will need a hemp warehouse or hemp manufacturing permit; i.e. a CCD licence does not substitute for an NMED hemp permit where hemp ingredients are handled - the permits stack; NMED FAQ, cultivation section, verbatim: If you perform extraction, process or manufacture hemp-derived material and/or hemp finish products, or store hemp extract a permit from NMED is required - even if you already hold an NMDA grower licence; third-party commentary asserting that intoxicating products must be sold through licensed dispensaries was not adopted because no CCD or RLD official page opened says soConfirmedhttps://www.env.nm.gov/hemp-rule-frequently-asked-questions/Retained.

4.14.42025 HB 346 (Hemp Products and Synthetic Cannabinoids) described as a proposal to prohibit sale of synthetic/semi-synthetic cannabinoids unless manufactured/sold by licensed cannabis businesses, with proposal status only, Verify, do not present as lawCorrectedhttps://www.nmlegis.gov/Sessions/25%20Regular/bills/house/HB0346CES.pdfCORRECTED STATUS: Died (API). HB 346, 57th Legislature, 1st Session, 2025, passed the House 54-7 on 13 March 2025 and passed the Senate 37-0 as amended on 22 March 2025, then Action Postponed Indefinitely, with no House concurrence recorded (nmlegis.gov legislation record: Current Location Died (API)). Its Fiscal Impact Report / committee-substitute synopsis describes NMED authority to regulate sale of hemp finished products and a prohibition on semisynthetic/synthetic cannabinoids - specifically, the House Commerce and Economic Development Committee substitute would have changed rulemaking authority from the Department of Environment to the Environmental Improvement Board, provided regulatory authority over hemp finished products at retail and semi-synthetic and synthetic cannabinoids, and banned receipt, possession, advertising, marketing or sale of semi-synthetic and synthetic cannabinoids. It did NOT make intoxicating hemp a CCD-licensed product, and it is NOT law. The original shorthand (unless manufactured/sold by licensed cannabis businesses) is removed.
