Research Notes — Both Runs (gaps, unverified items, conflicting figures, follow-ups)

How this section works. This is the combined research notes section required at the end of Run 2. It does not replace the Verify / Unavailable register at the end of each part — those registers are preserved in full in the body above and are the authoritative item-by-item lists. This section groups the material that matters most across both runs, so a reader does not have to hunt through seven registers to find what is still unsettled. Nothing in this section upgrades a Verify item to confirmed.

1. Gaps — what was not found, and what route was tried

  • No official statewide list of local cannabis rules (RLD/CCD/TRD checked, Part 3). Part 3 therefore gives jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction findings; several listed jurisdictions had no ordinance located in Run 1 (Clovis/Curry, Alamogordo/Otero, Carlsbad/Eddy, Raton, Torrance County) — that is a search result, not proof that no rule exists.
  • No downloadable bulk CCD licence register found (Part 5): CCD CROP is interactive only, the licence verification search is interactive only, and no bulk register was found. Licence totals therefore rest on dated snapshots (approvals to 4 Dec 2024; premises June 2025), not a live count.
  • No public NMDA grower/breeder/testing/nursery list found (Parts 5, 7): NMDA directs enquirers to Public Records requests. NMED's permitted-facilities list (updated 26 Oct 2026) and approved-lab list (updated 8 Sep 2026) do exist.
  • NMED hemp-facility count at audit (Part 7): 36 facilities on the official NM Approved Hemp Facilities list dated 26 October 2026 (19 manufacturing-type, 17 warehouse-type and 1 extraction facility, with one combined facility counted once). No official 2026 NMDA grower count; hemp acreage for 2023–2025 withheld/unavailable.
  • No official Texas-buyer or out-of-state-buyer share found (Parts 6, 10). CROP records sale location, not buyer residence. City totals (Sunland Park, Chaparral, Santa Teresa, Las Cruces) are reported, but the secondary “38% non-resident” claim is not adopted. No official city sales figures were found for Anthony (NM), Clovis, Hobbs or Farmington.
  • No official cumulative expungement total as of 31 Oct 2026 found (Parts 9, 12) after trying nmcourts, AOC, DPS, MPP and CCRC sources. Last dated count: ~14,000 cases expunged as of April 2023 (AOC General Counsel via secondary reporting). The 2022 DPS review pool (~151,640–155,000 cases) is a review pool, not completions, and must not be quoted as expungements.
  • No New Mexico-specific cannabis poll from 2024 or 2025 found (Part 9). Older polls are reported with sponsor/wording caveats only.
  • No full IGA texts confirmed public (Parts 5, 10): Picuris and Pojoaque agreements (25 Mar 2022) are announced and summarised secondarily, but no official downloadable text was found, so no IGA term is quoted as text in this dossier. A mirrored PDF on an unrelated domain was not relied on.
  • No verbatim tribal ordinance text opened for any of the 23 tribal governments (Part 10). For the 20 governments without a sourced IGA, the file records “no IGA, no tribal cannabis law/operation found — Verify”, which is neither a ban finding nor permission.
  • No current named CCD testing-lab list beyond a single hold-document number (Part 11): only Bluebonnet Labs, LLC TSTL-2024-0004-PRM-0001 is confirmed on an official CCD document, and its hold continued — Bulletin 25-19 (13 November 2025) plus a Permanent Restraining Order, Case No. D-202-CV-2025-00809: unretested product may not enter the market under any circumstances.
  • No CCD insurance or surety-bond dollar minimum found (Part 11); no CCD discount/sampling/giveaway rule found; no confirmed NMSU or UNM CCD Tier I–III licence; no NM veterinary-cannabis or pet-CBD rule located; no official operating Type I/II consumption-area count.
  • No dedicated hemp-only zoned property with a street address found on the listing sites searched (Part 8); no address-identified dedicated live listing found in Farmington, Roswell or Las Vegas (NM) on those sites.
  • No New Mexico statute, rule or agency guidance specifically responding to the federal hemp dates (12 Nov / 11 Dec 2026) found in NMED/NMDA/nmlegis sources to 31 Oct 2026 (Parts 1, 7, 10). This is the most time-sensitive follow-up in the dossier: New Mexico's 20 mg/package cap is 50× the federal 0.4 mg/container cap, so state compliance does not guarantee federal compliance after 11 Dec 2026.

2. Unverified items — the highest-priority follow-ups

  • NMOneSource direct re-check of all statute quotations (Parts 0–1, 2–3, 4, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12): much statute text was read on Justia/LawServer/Cornell mirrors. Before republication as confirmed, re-open each cited NMSA section on NMOneSource and each NMAC section on SRCA, including §§26-2C-41, 76-24-2, 76-24-8, 7-2-2/7-2A-2 (§280E decoupling subsection numbering), 7-9-73.2, 30-31-2(T), 26-2C-26, 66-8-102 and 22-33-5.
  • Tribal “state-licensed” question (federal Schedule III / §280E): whether any medical activity by a tribal operation under an intergovernmental agreement counts as “state-licensed” under 91 FR 22714. §26-2C-41 does not deem IGA activity state-licensed and does not address federal scheduling. Do not assume it either way.
  • Whether pueblo sales enter CROP/TRD totals, pueblo tax rates, testing/labelling/packaging, NMS2S tracking, CCD-licensee trade in either direction, tribal regulator names/structures, and who may buy from a pueblo enterprise (Part 10) — none found in an opened official source.
  • HB 346 (2025) final disposition (Parts 4, 7): Died — Action Postponed Indefinitely — after passing the House 54–7 on 13 March 2025 and the Senate 37–0 as amended on 22 March 2025, with no House concurrence recorded. It is not law; the NMED/EIB transfer it proposed never took effect.
  • NMDA varietal fee (Part 7): the 2026 Annual form was directly opened at audit — $650 + $6.00/acre + $10/variety — against the posted rule ceilings ($800 Annual / $900 Continuous). Only the legal basis of the $10 varietal minimum, against the rule's $25 per variety in excess of one, remains Verify.
  • NMED final-rule paragraphs for fees/terms/transfers (Part 7, 20.10.2.8(D)): confirmed from the published final rule at audit — extraction/manufacturing/warehouse $1,000, retail manufacturer $500, late $200, reinspection $500, variance $300, anniversary-month expiry, non-transferability.
  • Hemp minimum age: no statewide minimum age for hemp finished products found in 20.10.2 (secondary statement only). The 21+ rule is a CCD cannabis rule and must not be imported into hemp.
  • Whether the converted-cannabinoid ban reaches pure retailers or imported products, and whether any CCD licence is required for intoxicating hemp (Parts 1, 4, 7): no official source opened states a CCD licence is required; the only official interaction found is NMED's statement that a CCD licensee handling hemp ingredients still needs an NMED hemp warehouse/manufacturing permit.
  • GRT charged on the excise-inclusive price (Part 2): resolved at audit — GRT excludes cannabis excise tax receipts from 1 July 2023 (TRD FYI-260, Rev. 07/2026, p. 4). The October 2025 “missing file” gap is deleted: the current TRD index lists October business activity under the November-2025 file. Still outstanding: the current TRD GRT schedule, §7-9-73.2 full text, DFA cannabis-excise-line scope, and a total/by-locality revenue figure summed from TRD monthly CAN files.
  • Local-code currency (Part 3): Bernalillo County, Doña Ana County, Las Cruces hours/Realize code, Rio Rancho, Sandoval County, Santa Fe city/county, Roswell, Chaves County, Farmington hours conflict (7–11 vs 8–8 in UDC excerpts), San Juan Ord. 120, Hobbs distances/hours, Lea County, Gallup buffers/hours, McKinley County, Sunland Park current code, Taos Ord. 25-04 final text, Las Vegas (NM) buffers/hours/fees, San Miguel County permanent ordinance, Los Alamos ch. 16.
  • Testing-rule currency (Part 11): the 31 August 2026 amendment (NM Register Vol. XXXVII, Issue 16) replaces the product categories in 16.8.7.15 Table 1; the pre-amendment table in the original Part 11 is obsolete and must not be used for a compliance decision. Heavy-metal/mycotoxin mandatory status after the amendment remains Verify. Also: current CCD testing-lab list and post-Feb 2025 Bluebonnet hold status; courier $10,000 vs proposed $5,000 cap and related 3 Sep 2025 hearing proposals; producer tiers after the §26-2C-40 repeal (31 Dec 2025); medical Personal Production Licence currency (legacy 7.34.4.8 text).
  • Checkpoint and federal-land detail (Part 10): CBP confirmation of checkpoint locations and seizure reports (early-2024 seizures, >$300,000 confiscation petition claim are secondary); whether Schedule III changes checkpoint treatment of medical product; per-installation policies for White Sands Missile Range, Holloman, Kirtland and Cannon (only the general federal-land prohibition is stated); LANL-specific policy (not opened).
  • Firearms (Part 12): 18 U.S.C. §922(g)(3) is unamended, and United States v. Hemani, 608 U.S. 772, decided 18 June 2026, did NOT strike it down (as-applied only). The ATF January 2026 interim final rule (91 FR 2698, eff. 22 January 2026) defines “unlawful user” as regular use over an extended period continuing into the present without a lawful prescription; Schedule III status alone does not remove the disability, and a New Mexico medical certification is not shown to be a federal “lawful prescription.” Final ATF Form 4473 status at 31 October 2026 remains Verify. No NM-specific patient firearms statute located.
  • HUD post-rescheduling position, hotel-room-as-residence, private/post-secondary school policies, and the §22-33-5 policy count (Part 12): all Verify/Unavailable as listed in Part 12's register.
  • Rate-limit artefacts: several Run 2 facts rest on search-indexed text because direct opens returned 429 errors and were not retried (NMDA Hemp Registration page, NMED Jan 2026 training presentation, §26-2B-5, nmcourts expungement page, 6.12.10 NMAC, LoopNet Alamogordo page, a batch of 420Property detail pages). Those facts are flagged in their parts and must be re-opened directly before being treated as confirmed.

3. Conflicting figures — what was adopted, what was rejected, what is still open

  • Calendar-2024 sales: $540m (CannBus calc.) vs $580m vs $590m (other secondary compilations citing CCD) — unresolved, and no official annual total is adopted for 2024. No source in either run explains the difference (rounding, restatement, or inclusion/exclusion). Do not publish a single 2024 total without this note. Verify against CROP's full monthly series.
  • Calendar-2025 sales: $567m (MJBizDaily) vs $568m (CannBus, rounded) — secondary only, and no official annual total is adopted for 2025. The $1m difference is treated as rounding/vintage. A third figure, $628m (CannaMLS newsletter, May 2026), conflicts with the near-consensus and is rejected as uncorroborated.
  • Cumulative cannabis excise tax: $142.42m vs $117.72m from two TRD aggregators — unresolved (Part 2); Motley Fool's “2025 $54,429,452” figure is rejected (scope undefined, matches neither General Fund nor gross CAN). No gross total-CAN or cannabis-only GRT total is adopted.
  • Licence counts — do not merge bases: 3,071 approvals to 4 Dec 2024 vs June 2025 premises (303 producers incl. 127 micro, 274 manufacturers, 687 integrated incl. 428 VICE + 259 micro, 317 stand-alone retail, 27 consumption, 7 testing, 0 research; couriers not published) vs a secondary “>1,050 retailers” claim (not reconciled, not adopted as a current total). Testing labs likewise: 6 approvals vs 7 premises vs seven labs across eight premises (Oct 2025 testimony).
  • Patient counts: latest official DOH figure at audit is August 2026, 60,501 (data as of 2 September 2026); July 2026, 60,400, is the prior month. Secondary mirror “active patient” figures (20,411–47,778) rejected as artefacts. Secondary January 2026 (65,215) and May 2022 peak (135,388) figures flagged Verify against DOH reports; a secondary September 2026 figure (60,720) would break the Jan–Jun decline and needs direct confirmation.
  • June 2026 transaction split (Part 6): dollar series reconciles exactly June→July, but the June transaction components (842,530 vs 918,523) do not sum to the headline — flagged, not resolved.
  • Price: no official CCD monthly flower-price series found. $4.04/g (down 61.92% from $10.61/g at April 2022 open) is a CPPC-for-CCD figure via a price tracker — report itself Verify. A $77.33/g figure was rejected as a parsing error. Average transaction values derived in Part 6 ($39.66 overall in July 2026) are arithmetic derivations from CROP dollars/counts, not CCD-published prices and not flower prices.
  • Retailers per capita 47 per 100,000 is MJBizDaily-stated (citing RLD, no calculation shown), not an official CCD rate, and no CCD saturation assessment was found.
  • Property prices/sizes (Part 8): 911 N Camino Del Pueblo, Bernalillo — $4,124,000 flyer vs $4,400,000 LoopNet record; 1100 2nd St NW — $1,000,000 vs $1,240,000; 214 Menaul Blvd NE sizes; Portales street number (1841 vs 1864) and APN conflict, price not captured. All flagged, none resolved. Table B “$1” prices are placeholders, not prices.
  • Buffers: Albuquerque retailer separation 660 ft is confirmed on the City's official page (600 ft superseded 3 August 2024). Sunland Park's 200-foot school/daycare rule and special-use requirement are confirmed on the City's own bilingual cannabis-business process document; hours and the June 2022 reduction remain secondary-reported. The state rule is a 300 ft ceiling, not a floor (§26-2C-12).
  • Producer tier lower bound and increments (Part 4): resolved at audit on current SRCA 16.8.8.9 text — Level 1 is 201–2,000 mature plants and increases are in 500-plant increments. The 401 lower bound and 1,000-plant increment were 13 January 2022 emergency-amendment figures only, superseded 22 March 2022. Section 26-2C-40 was NOT repealed on 31 December 2025: the scheduled repeal was itself repealed by Laws 2024, ch. 38, §19, so the tiers stand under a live statute.
  • Reciprocity citation (Part 12): settled at audit as 7.34.3.22 (DOH “7.34.2.22” is an error). Consumption-area server-permit rule citation settled at audit as 16.8.10 NMAC (the “18.8.10” rendering was an error); consumption-area fee is $2,500/year under 16.8.11.9(J).
  • Ballot wording variant (Part 9): Bernalillo County 2014 advisory question (“$25 fine” vs “efforts to decriminalise”) — SOS results pages not opened, Verify.
  • Navajo/Estancia separation (Part 10): the 2025 Benally-linked Estancia raid is off Navajo land and is kept separate from both the Navajo raids and the Sept 2026 RLD Estancia raid; whether the two Estancia properties are the same is Verify, not asserted.
  • 2025 sales-tax stacking / medical GRT shorthand (Part 1): “exempt” shorthand rejected in favour of RLD's “file then deduct” mechanism for GRT; NMED hemp-rule date 1 Aug 2025 adopted over a 1 Sept 2025 variant; a Sept 2026 kratom special session reported elsewhere was North Dakota, not New Mexico, and is excluded.

4. Recommended follow-ups, in priority order

  1. Before 11 December 2026: check NMED, NMDA, RLD/CCD and nmlegis.gov for any New Mexico response to the federal hemp definition and 0.4 mg/container cap, and for any guidance on tribal medical activity under Schedule III. These are the two items in this dossier most likely to change compliance advice on a fixed date.
  2. NMOneSource + SRCA re-check of every statute and rule cited from a mirror, in the order listed in §2 above, and re-open every 429-affected page directly.
  3. CROP on publication day: recheck the live CROP headline, the Aug–Sep 2026 monthly postings, the full monthly series (to resolve 2024 and the June 2026 transaction split), and the CCD licence verification search for a current by-type active count.
  4. TRD: sum the monthly CAN distribution files (resolving the October 2025 gap) for total and by-locality revenue; confirm the GRT-on-excise question and the §7-9-73.2 text; ask TRD for post-Apr 2026 dual-licensee and tribal allocation guidance.
  5. Direct requests: Governor's office / RLD for IGA texts and terms; each pueblo's clerk/government for tribal cannabis laws and regulators; OSE for a cannabis water-enforcement docket or count; AOC/DPS for an updated expungement total; DOH for the September 2026 patient report and the January 2026 / May 2022 reports behind the secondary figures.
  6. Local codes: re-open the current code text for every jurisdiction listed as Verify in Part 3, and search Clovis/Curry, Alamogordo/Otero, Carlsbad/Eddy, Raton and Torrance County again by ordinance number rather than keyword.
  7. CBP and installations: check CBP releases for checkpoint seizure policy and each military installation / LANL for a published cannabis order before stating anything beyond the general federal-land prohibition.
  8. ATF / HUD: check for a final Form 4473 and a post-rescheduling HUD statement before advising any patient on firearms or federally assisted housing.
  9. Listings: re-check every Part 8 listing for live status, price and water rights on the listing date of use; listing status is Verify unless the listing itself shows it is active and recent.

Bottom line. The settled core of this dossier — both markets legal, the excise step-up schedule, the licence types and plant tiers, the water-proof rule, the NMED hemp rule and NMDA state plan, the July 2026 sales figures as secondary-reported (not official CROP totals), the August 2026 patient figure, the 3,071 approvals snapshot as a secondary figure with a date conflict (May/June 2026 vs 4 December 2024, neither adopted as official), the Picuris/Pojoaque IGAs and the dormant interstate section (§26-2C-38) — is consistent across both runs. Everything listed above is the remainder: flagged, not hidden, and each item names the exact source that would settle it.

Complete dossier — Parts 0–12. Research date 31 October 2026. See the Research Notes section above for gaps, unverified items, conflicting figures and follow-ups.
